name: Segub
overview: Segub was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified as the son of Hezron and the father of Jair. His lineage is briefly noted in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles, emphasizing his place within the family line of Judah. Beyond these familial connections, there are no additional notes or distinguishing events recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Segub means "exalted" in Hebrew. It is a proper name mentioned in Scripture without indication that it was given by God. This meaning may reflect a status or hope associated with his family line but is not explicitly connected to any divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Segub as the son of Hezron and the father of Jair, establishing his position within a generational line in the tribe of Judah. These relationships are explicitly noted in 1 Chronicles 2:21-22. No other family relationships are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Segub's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical framework of Judah's descendants. His mention as both son and father situates him in the continuity of God's covenant people, highlighting the faithfulness of lineage preservation. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on heritage and God's providential preservation of His chosen tribe.
